title: Complete and incomplete combustion
examples: What is the difference between complete and incomplete combustion?
Why is a Bunsen flame blue?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Let air in for a clean blue flame

explain.say: Look at a gas cooker flame: neat and blue. Now think of a candle: yellow and a bit smoky. Both are burning fuel, so why so different? Look at the board. You can see the two kinds of burning side by side.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Let air in for a clean blue flame

explain.say: See the left side? When a fuel like methane gets plenty of oxygen, it burns completely, with a hot blue flame. Combustion means burning. The carbon becomes carbon dioxide, and the hydrogen becomes water. What do you think happens with too little oxygen?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Let air in for a clean blue flame

explain.say: Look at the right side. With too little oxygen, burning is incomplete. The flame turns yellow and smoky, making soot, which is tiny bits of carbon, and a poisonous gas called carbon monoxide. Have you seen black soot under a pot?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Let air in for a clean blue flame

explain.say: Look at the reasons on the board. Carbon monoxide has no colour or smell, and it sticks to your red blood cells far more strongly than oxygen. So your body is starved of oxygen. That is why homes fit carbon monoxide alarms. Does your home have one?

because.note: You cannot see or smell it.

draw.answer: It silently stops your blood carrying oxygen

explain.say: Great work! Look at the energy picture: a good modern gas boiler, burning completely, sends about 90 percent of the fuel energy into heating water. Wow: incomplete burning wastes energy as unburnt soot, so a blue flame is safer and cheaper for you!

faq.a: Complete combustion is burning with plenty of oxygen. A hydrocarbon fuel makes only carbon dioxide and water, with a clean blue flame.
Incomplete combustion is burning with too little oxygen. It makes carbon monoxide and soot as well as water, with a yellow, smoky flame.
It has no colour or smell, and it binds to the haemoglobin in red blood cells, stopping them carrying oxygen. It can cause drowsiness and even death.
asks: Why do houses need carbon monoxide alarms?

faq.q: Why is a Bunsen flame blue when the air hole is open?
faq.a: Opening the air hole lets in plenty of oxygen, so the gas burns completely and very hot. With the hole closed, burning is incomplete, giving a yellow, sooty flame.

faq.q: What is the equation for methane burning completely?
faq.a: Methane plus oxygen gives carbon dioxide plus water: CH4 + 2O2 gives CO2 + 2H2O.

facts: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon produces only carbon dioxide and water.
Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin over 200 times more strongly than oxygen does.

quiz.say: Which gas is made by incomplete combustion but not by complete combustion?
quiz.show: Which gas is made by incomplete combustion but not by complete combustion?
quiz.why: With too little oxygen, some carbon only gets one oxygen atom, forming carbon monoxide.

wrong.0: Carbon dioxide is the main product of complete combustion.
wrong.1: Water vapour forms in both types.

quiz.say: A Bunsen burner gives a yellow, sooty flame. What should you do?
quiz.show: A Bunsen burner gives a yellow, sooty flame. What should you do?

options.show: Turn off the gas and add water
options.say: Turn off the gas and add water

options.show: Open the air hole to let in more oxygen
options.say: Open the air hole to let in more oxygen

quiz.why: More oxygen gives complete combustion and a clean blue flame.

wrong.0: Water is not needed; just let more air in.
wrong.2: Closing it reduces oxygen and makes the flame sootier.
